title: Thai Airways Warns 60,529 Passenger Booking Records May Have Been Accessed in Amadeus Security Incident
html:
Thai Airways has disclosed that approximately 60,529 passenger booking records may have been accessed without authorisation in a security incident involving Amadeus, the airline’s passenger-service technology provider. The airline said the incident affected data held in Amadeus systems between 10 August 2023 and 23 September 2026. It stated that its own systems and flight operations were not affected.

What information may have been accessed?

According to Thai Airways’ notice of 9 November 2026, the potentially accessed records may include passenger names, booking references (PNRs), travel dates, flight routes and cabin class. The airline also identified approximately 376 additional records that may contain further details, including email addresses, telephone numbers, passport numbers, nationality, frequent-flyer numbers, flight numbers, ticket numbers and seat numbers.

Thai Airways said credit-card information was not affected and that, as of the date of its notice, it had not found evidence that the information had been disclosed. The airline is continuing to review information supplied by Amadeus and says it will contact affected passengers individually after verification.

Did the incident affect flights?

The airline said the incident did not affect its own IT systems or operations. Thailand’s Civil Aviation Authority (CAAT) also said the information available to it indicated no impact on flight safety or airline services. The issue concerns the security of booking information, not a reported disruption to flight operations.

What should travellers do?

  • Watch for unexpected emails, calls or messages referring to a booking, itinerary or ticket.
  • Do not share passwords, one-time codes, passport scans or payment details in response to unsolicited messages.
  • Verify any request through the airline’s official website or customer-service channels rather than links in an unexpected message.
  • If you receive a notification from Thai Airways, follow the airline’s instructions and contact it through an official channel if anything is unclear.

Amadeus said it had addressed the vulnerability, revoked credentials associated with the unauthorised access and strengthened monitoring and detection. Its investigation and Thai Airways’ assessment remain ongoing.
